invariant_review_justification: The release publishes derived compliance values (framework readiness percentages, per-test pass/fail counters) and a generated artifact (web/dist) that is committed and served directly. Each has a repository-owned command that recomputes it from its authoritative source and compares.

contracts.authoritative_source: Docker Hub registry-1.docker.io library/node manifest for tag 24-slim
reject_conditions: Registry returns a digest different from the pinned value at deploy time
Image cannot be pre-pulled onto nas1 before app.create
Compose references a floating tag rather than the pinned digest

live_probe.observed_semantics: Valid tag answers HTTP 200 and carries a docker-content-digest header; the header is the immutable image identity used in compose.

negative_control.input: library/node manifest for the nonexistent tag 22-slim-does-not-exist-xyz
negative_control.observed_result: HTTP/2 404 with no docker-content-digest header, unambiguously different from the 200+digest answer for a real tag

contracts.authoritative_source: node:sqlite DatabaseSync API inside the pinned runtime image
contracts.version: Node v24.19.0 (stable node:sqlite, no flag, no ExperimentalWarning)
reject_conditions: require('node:sqlite') throws or needs --experimental-sqlite in the pinned image
The application test suite does not pass inside the pinned image on linux/amd64
The image emits an ExperimentalWarning for SQLite, indicating an unstable API contract
contracts.validation_command: docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/app:ro -w /app node:24-slim@sha256:3638d9a6fe4030bd716be989438248074489337ba3275657f93595428be4fc03 node --test tests/http.test.mjs tests/api.test.mjs
contracts.evidence: node v24.19.0; DatabaseSync=function with no warning; 22/22 tests pass inside the pinned image on linux/amd64 with the source mounted read-only, which is the production shape.

live_probe.command: docker run --rm node:24-slim@sha256:3638... node -e "require('node:sqlite')" plus the full suite under a read-only mount
live_probe.observed_semantics: node:sqlite is available unflagged and stable on Node 24; the server boots, seeds and serves with /app mounted read-only.

negative_control.observed_result: Node v22.23.2 also exposes DatabaseSync but prints 'ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time'. The probe therefore distinguishes a stable runtime from an experimental one, and node 22 was rejected as the base image because of it.

contracts.authoritative_source: TrueNAS SCALE middleware on nas1 via midclt over the ssh alias
reject_conditions: midclt is unreachable over the recorded transport
app.create or app.start returns a failed job
pool.dataset.query cannot distinguish an existing dataset from a nonexistent one
contracts.validation_command: ssh -o ConnectTimeout=25 -o BatchMode=yes nas1 "midclt call pool.dataset.query '[[\"name\",\"=\",\"TailsPool\"]]'"
contracts.evidence: nas1.insta.host reachable over the estate LAN; TailsPool returns one dataset row with parsed available/used properties.

live_probe.command: midclt call pool.dataset.query for TailsPool (valid) and for TailsPool/definitely-not-a-dataset-xyz (invalid)
live_probe.observed_semantics: A matching query returns a one-element array carrying available/used; the API is therefore usable as the capacity authority.

negative_control.observed_result: Empty array [] versus a one-element array for the real dataset, so presence and absence are distinguishable

reject_conditions: Token status is not active
Token lacks Access application, policy, tunnel configuration or DNS edit permission
Credential must be typed by an operator rather than read from the approved store
contracts.evidence: http=200 success=True status=active; credential sourced from ~/.config/cloudflare/env and never echoed.

live_probe.command: GET /user/tokens/verify with the real credential, then with a deliberately invalid one
live_probe.observed_semantics: A valid token returns HTTP 200 with success=true and status=active.

negative_control.observed_result: HTTP 400 with success=false and error code 6003, clearly different from the 200/active answer

reject_conditions: An ingress rule for vantage.insta.host already exists and points elsewhere
The catch-all rule is not last after the update
Ingress is added before the Access application and policy exist
contracts.validation_command: GET /accounts/{account}/cfd_tunnel/{tunnel}/configurations and assert the vantage rule precedes the catch-all
contracts.evidence: 43 existing rules, no vantage.insta.host rule present, so the hostname is free to claim.

live_probe.command: GET tunnel configurations for the real tunnel, then for 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
live_probe.observed_semantics: Returns config.ingress as an ordered array ending in a catch-all; order is significant and the catch-all must remain last.

negative_control.observed_result: HTTP 404 success=false error 1055, distinct from the 200 + ingress array for the real tunnel

contracts.version: Cloudflare API v4 zone record set
reject_conditions: vantage.insta.host already resolves to something else
DNS is created before the Access application, policy and tunnel ingress exist
The record is not proxied through Cloudflare
contracts.evidence: vantage.insta.host currently has 0 records, so the name is unclaimed.

live_probe.command: GET dns_records for books.insta.host (known-existing) and nonexistent-probe-xyz.insta.host (known-absent)
live_probe.observed_semantics: An existing name returns exactly one CNAME record; an absent name returns an empty result array.

negative_control.observed_result: 0 records versus 1 CNAME for books.insta.host. An earlier attempt used the unclaimed target hostname as the positive case, which returned 0 records for both inputs and could not distinguish success; the probe was re-run against a known-existing record to make it meaningful.

reject_conditions: Port 30002 appears in app.used_ports at deploy time
The port is outside the estate range 30000-32000
Allocation is asserted from repository configuration rather than the platform API
contracts.validation_command: ssh nas1 "midclt call app.used_ports" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; assert 30002 not in [p["port"] if isinstance(p,dict) else p for p in json.load(sys.stdin)]'

resource.limit_source: midclt call app.used_ports against the estate range 30000-32000

live_probe.observed_semantics: Returns the platform's own list of ports already bound by applications; this is the allocation authority, not a generic socket probe.

negative_control.input: Assert that a known-occupied port (30000, held by an existing estate app) is reported as used
negative_control.observed_result: 30000 is present in the returned list while 30002 is absent, so the table distinguishes occupied from free

contracts.authoritative_source: midclt call pool.dataset.query TailsPool available property
reject_conditions: Available space at deploy is below the requested size plus the safety margin
Capacity is asserted from repository configuration rather than live ZFS properties
Pool usage would exceed 75 percent of capacity after the release
contracts.evidence: 571475603376 bytes (532 GiB) available against a request of roughly 6 MB of release source plus a small SQLite database.

resource.limit_source: ZFS available property on TailsPool read live through the TrueNAS middleware

live_probe.command: midclt call pool.dataset.query for TailsPool with the available property
live_probe.observed_semantics: Returns parsed byte counts for available and used directly from ZFS.

negative_control.observed_result: Empty array rather than a row with byte counts, so a missing dataset cannot be mistaken for a healthy one

contracts.authoritative_source: Compose specification and the running container reported by app.get_instance
reject_conditions: Deployed image digest differs from the pinned digest
RELEASE_SHA reported by /healthz differs from the deployed commit
The application source mount is writable rather than read-only
The release carries any secret, since the service has no external dependency requiring one
contracts.validation_command: ssh nas1 "curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30002/healthz" and midclt call app.get_instance vantage
contracts.evidence: Identity surface proven wired to deployment inputs before freeze: booting with APP_VERSION/RELEASE_SHA/SOURCE_DIGEST set made /healthz report exactly those values (version 9.9.9, release_sha test000..., source_digest sha256:test in tests/api.test.mjs), and booting without RELEASE_SHA reported 'unversioned'. The deployed values are revalidated against the real commit and image digest at step 7 of the deployment.

live_probe.command: GET /healthz on the origin after deployment
live_probe.observed_semantics: Pre-deployment dry run on the workstation returned status ok with version, release_sha and source_digest sourced from the environment, proving the identity surface is wired to the deployment rather than hardcoded.

negative_control.input: Start the server without RELEASE_SHA set
negative_control.observed_result: /healthz reports release_sha 'unversioned' rather than a commit SHA, so an unlabelled deployment is detectable rather than silently passing

contracts.authoritative_source: package.json dependencies and the import statements in server/*.js
reject_conditions: package.json declares any runtime dependency
A server module imports a bare specifier that is not a node: builtin
contracts.evidence: PASS runtime_dependency_free. Proven able to fail: re-adding express to dependencies produced FAIL declared=[express].

invariant.derived_representation: package.json dependencies map, and the deployment assumption that no npm install runs on the host

reject_conditions: Rebuilding web/dist from web/src produces different bytes than the committed dist
web/dist is missing from the release commit
contracts.evidence: Rebuild leaves git status for web/dist clean, so the committed artifact is reproducible from the committed source.

invariant.derived_representation: web/dist committed to the repository and bind-mounted read-only into the container

contracts.authoritative_source: controls, tests, control_requirements and requirements tables
reject_conditions: A published framework readiness percentage differs from an independent recomputation
A framework's mapped control count differs from the mapping tables
contracts.evidence: All 7 frameworks agree with independent recomputation from the mapping tables.

invariant.authoritative_source: control_requirements joined to requirements, with per-control test status
invariant.derived_representation: readiness percentage published on the dashboard, framework pages and the public Trust Center

contracts.authoritative_source: test_entities rows written by the monitoring engine
reject_conditions: A test's stored passing_count or failing_count differs from its recorded entities
A test references a control that does not exist
contracts.evidence: 49 tests agree with their recorded entities; every test maps to an existing control.

invariant.derived_representation: tests.passing_count and tests.failing_count, surfaced throughout the UI and the Trust Center
